What each letter is, which is what really sticks here: $i$ and $j$ stay still — they say which cell of the result you are working on — and $k$ is the one that moves, running along the row and down the column at once. Y queda la pregunta buena: <em>¿por qué: And the good question remains: why on earth is it defined that way? Multiplying cell by cell would be easier to write, but it would be no use for anything. A matrix is not just any table of numbers: it is a transformation — a rotation, a stretch, a projection — and multiplying two matrices means applying one transformation after the other. If you do the arithmetic of chaining two transformations, what comes out is exactly this row-by-column rule. Nobody chose it: it came out.
